summary: The shared contract says both platforms dispatch the author with a parent-minted broker capability and that every file change goes through the author-broker write tool. Only the Claude agent carries that rule. The Codex TOML never mentions the capability or the broker tool, runs with workspace-write, and states the output-path limit as prose only.
proposed_fix: Add the capability input and the broker-only write rule to the Codex TOML, or state in formal-methods.md that Codex confinement is prose-only and record the reason in agent_inventory.json.

summary: Tool versions and checksums are hand-copied into engine.py, setup-formal-tools.py, catalog.py, quint.py, the JSON schema, package.json and several docs. No test asserts that setup TOOLS agree with engine CHECKER_SHA256 or catalog VERSIONS. The values agree today, so a version bump can drift silently.
proposed_fix: Make one module the pin source and import it in setup-formal-tools.py and engine.py, or add one test that compares all copies including the schema consts.

summary: formal-setup.md says the example catalogs default heap_mb to 4096, but the TLC example sets 1024. Example catalogs point at .specify/tools/apalache-0.62.2/lib/apalache.jar and .specify/tools/tla2tools-1.7.4.jar, while the setup script installs under .specify/tools/formal/<tool>-<version>/. The Quint catalog snippet copies to formal/counter, the directory the TLA counter step already uses, and counter-quint ships no catalog.
proposed_fix: Align the example catalog paths and heap values with the setup script output, correct the 4096 claim, and give the Quint example its own catalog and model directory name.

summary: The trace-layer evidence says native TLC trace qualification passed 26/26. The acceptance table (A4) and the delivery row for PR 563 both record TLC 27/27 on the same hosted run.
proposed_fix: Reconcile the count to the hosted run, or label 26/26 as the earlier layer-5 figure.

summary: plan.md still has four unchecked items (T5, T6, T6, and the full-harness review) for work that tasks.md marks complete (T5, T5a, T6, T6a, T6b) and acceptance.md A7 records as finished.
proposed_fix: Check the plan items or drop the duplicated checklist from plan.md so tasks.md is the only status record.

summary: stack-uat.md cites raw evidence under macOS temp directories that no reader can open. AGENTS.md says the privacy scan rejects macOS temp paths, but TMP_TRANSCRIPT_PATTERN only matches the Claude-specific temp prefix, so these paths pass the scan.
proposed_fix: Drop the temp-directory paths from the record (the results are already summarized), and widen the privacy pattern if temp paths are meant to be rejected.

summary: The audit says all current source hashes match its frozen inventory and source_drift_at_review is false. Eight of the eleven listed test scripts (including test-formal-checkers, -setup and -traces) no longer hash to their recorded frozen_sha256, and the counted-unit totals are stale with them.
proposed_fix: Mark the record as a dated snapshot, or refresh hashes and counts. Do not let the wording claim current-state agreement.

summary: The formal package holds autopilot policy: apply_resume_guard edits resume parse and signal dicts, gate_checkpoint knows gate ids G3 to G7, and required_checkpoints hardcodes autopilot Post step names. Modules also import each other lazily (helper and lifecycle, catalog and traces or native_config) to hide cycles.
proposed_fix: Move resume, gate and step-name policy next to resolve-autopilot-stage or validate-gate and have it call a small formal API. Give catalog validators a leaf module so the imports stop cycling.

summary: The shared workflow template says the Post closeout has 11 items. The Codex canonical list has 14 rows, adding Final Reviewability Backstop and PR Packet/Body Generation. The template's Post table carries neither row, so a Codex workflow starts with a checklist that disagrees with its own canonical plan.
proposed_fix: Give the Codex scaffold path a documented row set, or add the two rows to the template with a note on which host uses them.

summary: The workflow template's domain signal table lists 12 domains. The checklist guide lists 15 (it adds integration, mobile-ux and reliability), so the two disagree on what to recommend. Separately, SPEC-MOC.md sets status to in-progress (hyphen), while the MOC guide names in_progress as the canonical value; normalize_status accepts both.
proposed_fix: Make the guide the single domain list and have the template point to it. Change the SPEC-MOC status to in_progress.
